Context: Human substantia nigra neurons
Assay: IHC; immunoblot; absorption and H-ferritin cross-reactivity controls
Specificity: Monoclonal reagent with target-specific controls
Review depth: Primary full text
Rationale: Human substantia nigra neurons contain FTMT protein. The 2017 study used two postmortem donors without neurological disorders, a monoclonal reagent, absorption controls and an H-ferritin cross-reactivity check. The later study includes control as well as hemorrhage cases.
Limitations: Small postmortem normal-donor panel; does not establish treatment toxicity. Normal neuronal protein conflicts with unrestricted reproductive targeting, even when bulk brain RNA is low. This is not evidence of an observed FTMT-directed treatment injury.

Context: Human brain white-matter and peripheral axons
Specificity: Concordant modalities attributed to ABCC11/MRP8 in the primary report
Review depth: Primary abstract
Rationale: Human brain RT-PCR, immunoblotting and immunofluorescence locate ABCC11 in white-matter and peripheral axons.
Limitations: Abstract-level acceptance for conservative exclusion; full reagent controls not independently reviewed. MRP8 aliases for S100A8 excluded. This supports exclusion from unrestricted gene-level reproductive targeting. The MRP8 search alias also names S100A8 in other papers; those hits are not ABCC11 evidence.

Context: Human adrenal cortex (Vital); non-tumor vascular smooth muscle also reported
Assay: IHC and immunoblot; peptide competition described
Specificity: Peptide-raised polyclonal; reported competition controls not shown
Review depth: Primary full text
Rationale: The 2006 dbpC/contrin study reports normal vascular smooth-muscle and adrenal-cortical staining. Its specimens include non-tumor surgical regions and autopsies; peptide-raised polyclonal antibodies were checked by immunoblot and peptide competition, with controls described but not shown.
Limitations: Non-tumor surgical and autopsy samples; not a cardiomyocyte finding. Modern orthogonal confirmation still desirable. The published non-reproductive protein conflicts with unrestricted inclusion. Vascular cells in myocardium must not be relabelled cardiomyocytes. Modern primary HPA records also contain discordant renal, neural and endocrine staining.

Context: Human kidney tubules and primary patient-derived proximal tubular cells
Assay: Reported tissue protein localization and functional tubular-cell study
Specificity: Gene-resolved renal protein role in the primary report
Review depth: Primary abstract
Rationale: The renal-endocytosis study reports CCDC158 protein in kidney tubules and functional evidence in patient-derived proximal tubular cells.
Limitations: Abstract-level acceptance for conservative exclusion; patient-derived cells are not a healthy-volunteer panel. Testis/renal isoforms unresolved. A reproductive gene-level label misses a renal protein role. An isoform-specific target would require its own normal-expression and sequence assessment.

Context: Differentiating normal human epidermal keratinocytes
Assay: Endogenous RNA/protein; two antibodies and protein-band mass spectrometry
Specificity: Orthogonal endogenous protein identification
Review depth: Primary full text and abstract
Rationale: The 2021 study shows endogenous RNA and protein in differentiating normal human epidermal keratinocytes, with two antibody preparations and protein-band mass-spectrometry checks. Retinal epithelial cell-line experiments are additional context, not proof of normal retina in vivo.
Limitations: In vitro differentiation state; retinal epithelial cell lines do not establish in vivo normal retina expression. Expression is not confined to permitted follicles or reproductive tissues; ordinary epidermal keratinocytes remain non-permitted. Genetic loss of function and killing expressing cells are different interventions.

Context: Human cerebellar Purkinje cells

Review depth: Primary abstract
Rationale: The original HCA587 study reports cerebellar Purkinje-cell staining with the TC-1 polyclonal reagent, conflicting with the current curated negative normal profile.
Limitations: Abstract does not settle reagent specificity; no demonstrated target-mediated clinical injury. A neural protein conflict warrants a hold, but the historical antibody result does not establish target-mediated clinical injury or resolve MAGE-family cross-reactivity.

Context: Adult human bladder and spleen; distinguish fetal/placental specimens
Assay: Historical PP13 immunoreactivity versus Northern/placental surveys
Specificity: Unresolved galectin cross-reactivity and anatomy
Review depth: Primary abstracts
Rationale: Early PP13 protein work reported extra-placental reactivity, whereas Northern analysis and later placental-galectin work support placental restriction. Adult bladder/spleen observations must be separated from permitted fetal tissues and possible galectin cross-reactivity.
Limitations: Adult versus fetal samples and original protein bands require full-paper adjudication. Conflicting assay identity is unresolved; neither a proven unsafe classification nor unconditional inclusion is justified by these abstracts alone.

Context: Human pancreatic duct cells; healthy versus cystic-fibrosis context

Limitations: Human pancreatic RNA is qualitative, not nTPM. Disease/cell-model functional experiments and mouse measurements do not establish healthy human protein abundance.
